This integration shows the data of your Volkswagen ID. electric cars (ID.3,
ID.4, ID.5, ID.7, ID. Buzz…) in Gladys. It uses Volkswagen's **EU Data Act
portal** with the account of the **Volkswagen** smartphone app. No box to
install.

> **Why the EU Data Act portal?** Since 2026-06-01, Volkswagen has closed to
> third-party applications the access the ID. app uses. The EU Data Act
> portal is the only source still open. It is **read-only**, and Volkswagen
> publishes a snapshot of the car there **every 15 minutes** at best. So the
> integration cannot start the charge or the climatisation, nor lock the
> car.

## What you get

One device per car linked to the portal, with:

| Value                   | Note                |
| ----------------------- | ------------------- |
| Battery level (%)       |                     |
| Range (km)              |                     |
| Charging                |                     |
| Charging power (kW)     |                     |
| Charging cable plugged  |                     |
| Charge limit (%)        |                     |
| Remaining charging time | only while charging |
| Outside temperature     |                     |
| Odometer                |                     |
| Door / window open      |                     |
| Locked                  |                     |

A value the car has not sent yet is left out.

## Step 1: enable the EU Data Act portal (once, in a browser)

1. Open [https://eu-data-act.drivesomethinggreater.com/](https://eu-data-act.drivesomethinggreater.com/) and sign in with the
   account of the Volkswagen app. Accept the terms if the portal shows them.
2. Go to **Data clusters → Vehicle overview**. If your car is not listed,
   click **Connect your car** and follow the steps.
3. Click **Get customised data**.
4. Tick the agreement under article 4 of the EU Data Act, then **Next**.
5. Tick **All data**.
6. Name the request, for example "Gladys".
7. Pick the **every 15 minutes** frequency and **no end date**.
8. Send the request.

The first data arrives 15 minutes to a few hours later. The car must be awake
to send any: drive, charge, or open the Volkswagen app.

## Step 2: configure the integration

1. In Gladys, open the **Configuration** tab of the integration and enter the
   **email address** and the **password** of the Volkswagen account.
2. The **refresh interval** sets how often new data is checked: every
   5 minutes by default, every 3 minutes at most. Volkswagen only publishes a
   snapshot every 15 minutes: going lower is pointless.
3. Save, then click **Test the connection**. The message lists the cars found
   and whether data is already available.
4. Add your cars from the **Discovery** tab.

The password stays in Gladys. The integration writes nothing to disk.

## Scenes

The integration adds its own cards to the scene editor (Gladys 5.1 or later),
under the **Integrations** category:

- **Charge completed** (trigger) — starts the scene when a car has finished
  charging because its battery reached the charge limit. Optionally pick the
  car. The following actions can read `{{triggerEvent.data.battery_level}}`
  and `{{triggerEvent.data.range}}`. With a snapshot every 15 minutes, the
  event can come up to a quarter of an hour after the charge actually ended.

The car values are regular Gladys devices too: a scene can, for example, warn
you when the car is left unlocked in the evening.

## Dashboard

Add the **Volkswagen ID.** widget to a dashboard and pick the car (the first
of the account by default). It shows the battery and the range live, and the
state of the charge, the cable, the locks and the openings. The **Refresh**
button checks right away whether Volkswagen published new data.

The **Volkswagen ID. picture** widget shows the same values around a picture
of your car. Volkswagen does not provide it to Gladys: the EU Data Act portal
has none, and the picture service of the Volkswagen app is closed to
third-party applications. Provide it yourself:

1. Take a picture of your car, for example a screenshot of the Volkswagen
   app, cropped to the car.
2. Reduce it to **300 KB at most**, as PNG, JPEG or WebP (Gladys refuses
   heavier images). A width of 800 pixels is enough.
3. Put it online at a public **https** address, for example in a GitHub
   repository (the file's "Raw" link).
4. Paste that address in the **Picture of the car** field of the
   Configuration tab, then save.

The integration downloads the picture once, without sending any Volkswagen
credential there. Without an address, the widget says so instead of showing a
generic image; when the picture cannot be shown (too heavy, address not
found…), the widget says so and the logs give the reason. With several cars on
the account, the same picture is used for all.

Both widgets show the name you gave the car when adding it to Gladys (else its
nickname in the Volkswagen app).

## Troubleshooting

- **"Volkswagen sign-in refused"** — check the email address and the password
  by signing in to the portal in a browser. After a refusal, the integration
  waits 15 minutes before trying again, so the account does not get locked.
- **"Sign in once to the Volkswagen EU Data Act portal…"** — the portal was
  never opened with this account, or it waits for you to accept its terms:
  do step 1.
- **"No data reaches Gladys yet: enable the continuous data request…"** —
  step 1 is not finished (points 3 to 8).
- **Values stuck** — the car is asleep and the portal only receives empty
  snapshots: values come back once the car drives or charges.

Diese Einstellungen fragt Volkswagen ID. in seinem Konfigurationsbildschirm in Gladys ab.

| Einstellung | Typ | Pflichtfeld | Beschreibung |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before you start: the Volkswagen EU Data Act portal | `section` | Nein | Volkswagen only shares the car's data through its EU Data Act portal, read-only, every 15 minutes. Once, in a browser: sign in to the portal with the account of the Volkswagen app, link your car, then request customised data with all data clusters, every 15 minutes, with no end date. Then enter the same email and password below. |
| Email address | `string` | Ja |  |
| Password | `secret` | Ja |  |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | Nein | How often each car's new data is checked, in seconds. Volkswagen publishes it every 15 minutes: three minutes minimum. |
| Picture of the car (optional) | `string` | Nein | https address of a picture of your car for the picture widget (PNG, JPEG or WebP, 300 KB max). Volkswagen does not provide it to Gladys. |

## So installierst du Volkswagen ID. in Gladys

1. Öffne in Gladys **Integrationen**: Volkswagen ID. erscheint im Katalog neben den nativen Integrationen, mit einem Community-Badge.
2. Klicke auf **Installieren**. Gladys lädt das Docker-Image (`ghcr.io/philippema/gladys-volkswagen:1.2.2`) herunter, startet es in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox und erzeugt die Oberfläche der Integration (Geräte, Erkennung und Konfiguration).
3. Öffne den Bildschirm **Konfiguration** der Integration, fülle die Einstellungen aus und speichere.
4. Du kannst sie auch direkt über die URL ihres Repositorys installieren: [https://github.com/PhilippeMA/Gladys-volkswagen](https://github.com/PhilippeMA/Gladys-volkswagen).

Volkswagen ID. benötigt Gladys `>=5.1.0`. Der Katalog in Gladys wird stündlich aktualisiert, eine neue Version ist also spätestens eine Stunde nach ihrer Veröffentlichung verfügbar.

Du nutzt Gladys noch nicht? Es ist kostenlos und Open Source: [folge der Installationsanleitung](/de/docs/), um loszulegen.

## Über externe Integrationen

Volkswagen ID. ist eine **externe Integration**: eine Community-Integration, die als Docker-Container verpackt und auf GitHub veröffentlicht wird. Gladys installiert sie mit einem Klick und führt sie in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox aus. Sie wird von [PhilippeMA](https://github.com/PhilippeMA) veröffentlicht und gepflegt, nicht vom Gladys-Kernteam.
